 Eternal’s ad and sales promotion expenses rise 41% to Rs 1,138 crore in Q2FY27
 The company also raised Blinkit’s store expansion target, reported growth across food delivery and District, and outlined how AI agents could reshape customer acquisition.
 afaqs! news bureau 
 21 Oct 2026 
 18:35
 IST Follow Us
 New Update Eternal, the parent company of Zomato, the food delivery platform, and Blinkit, the quick-commerce platform, reported advertisement and sales promotion expenses of Rs 1,138 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 41.2% from Rs 806 crore in the year-ago quarter.
The expense was also up 20.4% from Rs 945 crore in the April-June quarter of FY27, according to the company’s financial results. Eternal has not separately disclosed how much of this expense went towards advertising, sales promotion or individual platforms.
The company’s Q2FY27 shareholder letter also flagged a possible change in how it acquires customers, as artificial intelligence (AI) agents become more capable of facilitating purchases. Deepinder Goyal, founder and vice-chairman of Eternal, said part of its digital marketing spend on new customer acquisition could move to AI agents, which may offer more targeted customer acquisition costs than the company currently gets from Google and Meta. 
 Blinkit raises store expansion target 
 Blinkit’s quick-commerce business added 308 net new stores during the quarter, taking its total store count to 2,751. Eternal now expects Blinkit to cross 3,500 stores by March 2027, higher than its earlier guidance of 3,000 stores. Its current plans point to around 5,000 stores by March 2028. 
 The company said new stores in smaller cities were reaching around 1,000 orders a day in a similar time frame to stores in metros, with average order values at 85-90% of metro levels. 
 Blinkit’s net order value (NOV) grew 79.3% year-on-year to Rs 20,940 crore in Q2FY27. Eternal said it expects adjusted EBITDA margins to improve as the network expands, with mature stores and cities helping offset the initial pressure from newer outlets. 
 The shareholder letter also discussed Blinkit’s approach to private labels and advertising. The company said it would rather use the platform’s shelf space and visibility to help third-party brands grow, allowing it to earn advertising revenue, than compete with those brands through its own labels. 
 “We don’t want to become both the platform and a competitor to the brands on the platform,” Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa said in the letter. 
 Food delivery returns to 20% growth range 
 Eternal’s food delivery business, operated through Zomato, recorded NOV of Rs 11,445 crore, up 21.5% year-on-year. Average monthly transacting customers grew 16% to 28 million. 
 Goyal said the business’s long-term expectation remained annual growth of more than 20%, adding that the last two quarters had brought it back into that range after a slowdown. He also noted that a growing share of new users were ordering food online for the first time, many of them outside the company’s top eight cities. 
 The food delivery business reported adjusted EBITDA of Rs 627 crore, up 25% year-on-year. Its adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 5.5% of NOV. 
 District grows faster than planned 
 District, Eternal’s going-out business spanning dining and entertainment ticketing, is another area to watch. The company said NOV growth was running at more than 50% year-on-year, ahead of the 30%-plus compound annual growth rate built into its FY30 plan. 
 Eternal said it remained on track with its earlier FY30 targets of Rs 28,000 crore in NOV and Rs 1,400 crore in adjusted EBITDA. It also reiterated its expectation of reaching adjusted EBITDA break-even in four to six quarters, guidance originally issued in January 2026. 
 The company’s update suggests that District is growing faster than initially anticipated, although it has not revised its long-term targets. 
 Hyperpure expands beyond restaurant ingredients 
 Hyperpure, Eternal’s business-to-business supply operation, now serves around 85,000 restaurants, up from 62,000 a year earlier. 
 The company said it now delivers within two hours in all major cities, with around a quarter of its orders already arriving within that window. It is also expanding beyond ingredients into services such as third-party logistics for large restaurant chains and helping restaurants set up complete kitchens, including sourcing equipment. 
 The business is positioning itself as a broader supply-chain partner for restaurants, rather than only a supplier of food ingredients. 
 Revenue grows, with a change in quick-commerce accounting 
 Eternal reported consolidated adjusted revenue of Rs 24,621 crore in Q2FY27, up 76% year-on-year. However, the company said like-for-like adjusted revenue growth was 58%, with the difference largely reflecting the shift to an inventory-led model in quick commerce. Under this model, revenue includes the full value of goods sold rather than primarily marketplace commissions. 
 The company’s consolidated business-to-consumer NOV grew 54% year-on-year to Rs 35,644 crore. Adjusted EBITDA rose 197% to Rs 666 crore.
